name: Eastern Redcedar

facts.how: A few dried and crushed as a juniper spice
facts.where: Old fields and fence rows across the eastern half

caution: Use only a few berries as a SEASONING, never as a food or in medicinal quantity; concentrated juniper is hard on the kidneys and unsafe in pregnancy. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: A dense evergreen with scaly foliage and waxy blue berries. Crush one: it smells of gin, because juniper is what makes gin.

sections.title: Uses
sections.body: A pinch of crushed dried berries seasons game and stews. This is a spice, not a snack.
